title: Rav Chana
author: Aharon Hyman

paragraphs: In [Shabbat 97a](https://www.sefaria.org/Shabbat.97a.20-21), Rav Chana transmits Rav Yehudah’s report in the name of Shmuel — Rav Chana sat and it was difficult for him — Rav Yosef said to him, “The Master teaches it on this…,” etc. But Tosafot’s reading there, 4b, s.v. Zarak, is “Rav Chisda sat.” In [Bava Batra 157a:9-11](https://www.sefaria.org/Bava_Batra.157a.9-11): “Rav Chana said: Come and hear — Rav Nachman said to him,” etc. Hyman cites Chullin 56b (compare [Chullin 56a:12](https://www.sefaria.org/Chullin.56a.12)): a certain hen at Rav Chana’s house — he sent it before Rav Mattenah, who declared it kosher. He said to him, “But Levi taught…” — he said to him, “There,” etc. Hyman suggests that perhaps he is Rav Chana, son-in-law of Rav Ada bar Ahavah, mentioned in [Yevamot 110b:12](https://www.sefaria.org/Yevamot.110b.12), where Rav Nachman said: “I found Rav Ada bar Ahavah and Rav Chana his son-in-law sitting and posing challenges to one another in the market of Pumbedita.”[^4]

notes.text: Saved Davidson Shabbat97b gives Rav Yosef’s statement, not a question. Saved Yevamot110b has posing challenges, not making pools. The possible Chana identification remains Hyman’s conjecture; רבי וסף is read Rav Yosef contextually.

The consulted Shabbat 97a–97b preserves Chana’s chain and Yosef’s declarative reply; the folio boundary separates them. Yevamot 110b directly names Chana, Ada bar Ahavah’s son-in-law, in a marketplace discussion. Hyman’s possible identification and the exact Tosafot Chisda reading remain separately attributed.

The consulted [Shabbat 97a:20–21](https://www.sefaria.org/Shabbat.97a.20-21) names Rav Chana in the chain and again as the person who raises a difficulty. [Heilprin’s entry](https://www.girsology.com/seder-hadorot.html?entry=1386&lang=en) records Maharshal’s Rav Chisda reading and also reports a different reading attributed to Rabbeinu Tam. Those are variant readings of the passage.

In Bava Batra, Chana cites the case of a collapsed house. The hen sent to Rav Mattenah is at Chullin 56a. Yevamot names a Rav Chana as Ada bar Ahavah’s son-in-law; Hyman proposes that the notices refer to the same person.
